# Introduction

## About this template

This template uses **Typst** instead of LaTeX to generate PDF output. Typst is a modern typesetting system that compiles much faster than LaTeX and does not require a TeX installation. The UHH design (colors, fonts, list markers, table styling) is preserved.

Configure the YAML header including the following elements:

- `title`: Title
- `subtitle`: Subtitle; remove option completely if you don't need a subtitle.
- `author`: Character of single or multiple author(s)
- `date`: A date
- `abstract`: The abstract will be shown right after the title in smaller font size.
- `language`: If language is NOT English refer to the file `custom_lang.yml` for automatic text in German.
- `bibliography`: A path to the bibliography file to use for references (BibTeX `.bib` file).
- `csl`: The style is provided in the 'sage-harvard.csl' file.
- `format - typst`: In this template the Quarto options for Typst output are listed in the YAML header. See the [Typst format reference](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/typst.html) for more options.
- `mainfont`: Choose between "Helvetica Neue" (default) and "TheSansUHH" (UHH members only).

The font is set when running the function, e.g., `UHHformats::create_quarto_doc(dirname = "my_doc", template = "typst_simple", font = "TheSansUHH")`.


## Advantages of Typst over LaTeX

- **No TeX installation required** -- Typst is bundled with Quarto (version 1.4+)
- **Much faster compilation** -- milliseconds instead of seconds
- **Simpler syntax** -- easier to customize templates
- All UHH design elements (colors, fonts, headers, list markers) are supported


## Code blocks

Code blocks work identically to other Quarto formats:

```{r}
#| eval: false
summary(cars)
```

# Methods

## Cross-references

Cross-references work as in other Quarto formats: `@fig-label` for figures, `@tbl-label` for tables, `@sec-label` for sections.

This is a cross-reference to @tbl-kable in @sec-tables and to @fig-base in @sec-figures.


## Mathematical equations

Use mathematics as usual with the dollar sign `$`: inline mode $E = mc^2$ or display mode: $$E = mc^2$$

# Results

## R output

```{r}
mtcars <- read.csv("data/mtcars.csv")
summary(mtcars[,1:4])
```


## Tables {#sec-tables}

### Using the *knitr* package

@tbl-kable is an example of using `knitr::kable()` to generate a table.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-kable
#| tbl-cap: "This is a table produced with knitr::kable()."
df <- mtcars[1:5, 1:6]
knitr::kable(df)
```


## Figures {#sec-figures}

A base graphics scatterplot (@fig-base).

```{r}
#| label: fig-base
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between horsepower and fuel economy."
plot(mtcars$hp, mtcars$mpg,
xlab = "Gross Horsepower",
ylab = "Miles Per Gallon",
pch = 19)
abline(lm(mpg ~ hp, data = mtcars), col = "red")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-boxplot
#| fig-cap: "Fuel differences between transmission types (0 = automatic, 1 = manual)."
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 3
boxplot(mpg ~ am, mtcars)
```


# Adding citations and bibliography

Link a `.bib` document via the YAML header. References can be cited using `[@key]`, e.g., [@Taylor1937]. Multiple entries: [@Knupp1999; @Kamm2000]. In-text: @Taylor1937.


## Software

All analyses were performed using the statistical software R (version `r paste(R.Version()$major, R.Version()$minor, sep = ".")`) [@R-base]. This document was generated using the R packages 'rmarkdown' (version `r packageVersion("rmarkdown")`) [@R-rmarkdown], 'UHHformats' (version `r packageVersion("UHHformats")`) [@R-UHHformats], and 'knitr' (version `r packageVersion("knitr")`) [@R-knitr].
